items.title: Vincent Pelote interviewed by Monk Rowe, Orlando, Florida, February 25, 2017
items.q: last Thursday before coming down here Valery Ponomarev... he had a group of kids... Valery is sitting next to me and he’s just laughing his butt off.

ctx.x: Close enough for jazz. Oh, I love talking to you. I’m not sure I can phrase this question, to sort of wrap up. You know we’ve been talking about the past and what’s your take on jazz in America now, considering record sales and jazz education and jazz as an art form. © Fillius Jazz Archive -18-

It’s all over the place right now. You know it’s interesting that you ask me the question because one of the thing that Ed and I — Ed Berger — I keep bringing his name up and I guess it’s because his death is still so fresh in my head. But he used to talk about the fact that we have this chancellor in Newark now, I used to say she’s new but she’s been here for a couple of years ago so she’s not that new anymore. And she’s been trying to use the Institute of Jazz Studies as a sort of a way to, I don’t know, to…
Can you tell me what MJPAC is?
